\[
W = \begin{bmatrix}
  10 & 20 & 30 \\
  40 & 50 & 60 \\
  70 & 80 & 90
\end{bmatrix}, \qquad \frac{1}{16} \sum K \odot W = \frac{800}{16} = 50
\]

Each value is multiplied by the weight on top of it: the center counts 4 times, the side neighbors twice and the corners once. The products add up to 800. Divided by the sum of the weights, 16, that gives 50.
